data.name: Mirrors - Tomblight Edition
data.detailed_description:
Mirrors é um jogo de quebra-cabeça que reflete a luz inspirado em The Mummy e o método egípcio antigo de refletir a luz com espelhos.

Você joga como um aventureiro procurando por um tesouro em uma grande quantidade de túmulos. Para navegar pelas tumbas, reflite os feixes de luz ao redor usando os espelhos que estão à sua disposição. Acerte o receptáculo com a luz e a porta do próximo túmulo se destrave. Quanto mais nas ruínas você se aventura, mais perigoso se torna. Superar obstáculos, evitar armadilhas e derrotar os inimigos ao tentar completar cada túmulo e recuperar as Frascos Canópicos.

Quando terminar de procurar o tesouro, existem outras maneiras de usar suas habilidades de aventura para um bom uso. Por que não se colocar no teste no modo cronometrado? Pense que você é melhor do que um faraó? Tente sua mão em criar seus próprios níveis com o Criador de Nível, então dirija-se ao Poço do Curador e mostre-os aos seus amigos.

Bom aventureiro de sorte!

data.short_description: Mirrors é um jogo de quebra-cabeça que reflete a luz, onde você joga como um aventureiro que atravessa os túmulos do antigo Egito. Ao refletir a luz nos espelhos em um receptáculo, você pode avançar mais profundamente para os túmulos onde o perigo aguarda. Você pode encontrar o tesouro do faraó?

movies.name: Mirrors - The Light Reflection Puzzle Game

reviews.review:
Mirrors - Tomblight Edition is a compact puzzle adventure that turns the simple act of reflecting light into an expedition through the tombs of Ancient Egypt. Developed and published by MONOCOOL, it combines traditional beam-routing puzzles with exploration, traps, enemies, collectibles, and a treasure-hunting theme. Rather than presenting its challenges as isolated logic boards, the game places them within ancient ruins where the player assumes the role of an adventurer searching for the Pharaoh's treasure. The concept is easy to understand, but the surrounding adventure elements give the puzzles enough personality to distinguish the experience from more abstract games in the genre.

The fundamental objective involves positioning and manipulating mirrors to redirect beams of light toward specific receptacles. Successfully illuminating the required target opens the way into the next tomb. The early stages allow plenty of room to understand how reflections behave, while subsequent areas introduce layouts that demand greater awareness of positioning and the available mirrors. There is satisfaction in examining a chamber, predicting the path that the beam needs to follow, and gradually assembling the correct solution. It favors observation and logical thinking rather than fast reactions, making it approachable for casual puzzle players while still offering situations that require careful planning.

Exploration becomes more dangerous as the adventure moves deeper into the ruins. Environmental obstacles and traps complicate otherwise straightforward routes, while enemies add another concern beyond solving the optical puzzles. Players can also search for Canopic Jars, giving completionists an additional reason to investigate each area instead of immediately rushing toward the exit. These elements are not intended to transform the game into a full-scale action adventure, but they successfully break up the puzzle solving and reinforce the idea that these tombs are dangerous places rather than decorative backgrounds.

The Tomblight Edition substantially improves the presentation and general experience. Enhanced lighting is especially valuable because light itself is central to both the puzzles and visual identity. The updated version also features upgraded visuals, redesigned mummies, refined traps, and improvements to progression. These changes give the older game a cleaner and more polished appearance without abandoning its straightforward design. The Egyptian atmosphere remains relatively modest in scope, but dark tomb interiors contrasted against bright beams of redirected light create an appropriate setting for the mechanics.

There is also more to do after progressing through the primary adventure. Timed challenges encourage players to approach familiar mechanics with greater speed and efficiency, changing the otherwise relaxed puzzle-solving rhythm. The Level Creator is an even more interesting addition because it allows players to design their own challenges. Building a functional mirror puzzle requires understanding the mechanics from a designer's perspective, potentially extending the game's lifespan for anyone who enjoys experimenting with layouts. The inclusion of 23 Steam achievements adds another layer of optional objectives for players interested in completing everything.

Its greatest weakness is that the central mechanic can inevitably become repetitive. Nearly everything revolves around manipulating reflected light, and players who are not particularly interested in spatial or optical puzzles may find that the additional traps and adventure components are not enough to maintain their enthusiasm. The action elements are supporting mechanics rather than deep systems of their own. Conversely, that focused design is also one of the game's strengths. It knows exactly what kind of experience it wants to provide and avoids burying its puzzles beneath unnecessary complexity.

Steam Deck compatibility is particularly good following the Tomblight Edition update, which introduced full Steam Deck support. The game's relatively lightweight technical demands and puzzle-oriented structure make it well suited to handheld sessions. Being able to work through individual tombs without needing an extended play session complements portable gaming nicely, while the updated support makes the Deck a practical way to experience the adventure.

Overall, Mirrors - Tomblight Edition is an enjoyable example of how a straightforward puzzle mechanic can become more engaging when placed inside a cohesive setting. Redirecting light remains the foundation of the experience, but treasure hunting, traps, enemies, Canopic Jar collection, timed challenges, achievements, and user-created levels prevent it from feeling completely one-dimensional. The improved visuals and progression of the Tomblight Edition also make this the preferable version for newcomers. It may not offer the complexity or production scale of a major puzzle adventure, but its focused mechanics and Ancient Egyptian theme give it a distinctive charm. For players who enjoy logical puzzles and methodical exploration, it offers a pleasantly specialized journey into the tombs.

Rating: 7/10
